dmTitle.infoName: Built-in Test (BIT/BITE) and System Test Procedures

proceduralStep.para: This data module provides procedures for executing Built-In Test (BIT) and Built-In Test Equipment (BITE) functions for the AMPEL360 Q100 Indicating and Recording System. BITE tests verify system functionality, isolate faults to line-replaceable units (LRUs), and validate interfaces.

proceduralStep.title: Power-Up BIT (Continuous BIT)
proceduralStep.para: Continuous BIT runs automatically whenever power is applied to the system. It monitors critical functions in real-time and generates fault codes if anomalies detected.
Apply aircraft power (BAT or external power).
Observe display units during power-up sequence. All displays should illuminate and show initialization screens within 10 seconds.
Monitor for BITE fault messages on maintenance pages. Navigate to: MFD → MENU → MAINTENANCE → BITE STATUS.
If fault codes present, record fault code numbers and refer to fault isolation procedures (DMC-AMPEL360-31-00-00-730A).

proceduralStep.title: Initiated BIT (On-Demand BITE)
proceduralStep.para: Initiated BITE tests are manually triggered to perform comprehensive system checks, including functions not continuously monitored.
Ensure aircraft is on ground with parking brake set and engines/motors secured.
Access BITE menu: MFD → MENU → MAINTENANCE → BITE TESTS.
Select test category: - Display System Tests - Alerting System Tests - Recording System Tests - Data Acquisition Tests - Interface Tests
Select specific test from list and press INITIATE button.
Observe test progress indicator. Tests typically complete in 30-120 seconds.
Review test results: - PASS: System function verified, no action required - FAIL: Fault detected, refer to fault code for corrective action - INCOMPLETE: Test could not complete, check prerequisites
Access display test menu: MFD → MENU → MAINTENANCE → DISPLAY TESTS.
Select "Color Bar Test" to verify display color rendering. Full-screen color bars (red, green, blue, white, black) should be clearly visible with no dead pixels or discoloration.
Select "Pixel Test" to check for stuck or dead pixels. Display shows white, black, and checkerboard patterns.
Select "Touch Screen Test" (if applicable) and touch indicated target points to verify touchscreen calibration and responsiveness.
Select "Brightness Test" and adjust brightness slider to verify backlight control through full range.
Access alerting test menu: MFD → MENU → MAINTENANCE → ALERT TESTS.
Select "Master Warning Test". Master Warning light should illuminate and aural warning tone should sound.
Select "Master Caution Test". Master Caution light should illuminate.
Select "Alert Display Test". Sample warning, caution, and advisory messages should appear on CAS display with correct color coding (red, amber, white).
Select "Aural Warning Test". System cycles through all aural warning types (gong, chime, voice alerts). Verify clear audio output.
Access recording test menu: MFD → MENU → MAINTENANCE → RECORDER TESTS.
Select "FDR Status Test". Display shows: - Recording status (RECORDING / FAULT) - Memory usage percentage - Last write time - BITE fault codes (if any)
Select "CVR Status Test". Display shows recording status, memory usage, and erase protection status.
Select "QAR Status Test". Display shows recording status and removable memory module presence.
WARNING: Do not initiate recorder write tests during normal operations. These tests are for ground maintenance only.
Access data acquisition test menu: MFD → MENU → MAINTENANCE → DATA ACQ TESTS.
Select "DAU Status Test". Display lists all Data Acquisition Units with status: - DAU-1 through DAU-4 - Communication status (ACTIVE / FAIL) - Parameter count - Built-in test results
Select specific DAU for detailed status including: - ARINC 429 port status - Analog input channel status - Discrete input status - Internal temperature and voltages
Access fault code history: MFD → MENU → MAINTENANCE → FAULT HISTORY.
Review active faults (currently detected) and logged faults (historical).
For each fault, note: - Fault code number - LRU identifier - Detection time/date - Flight phase when detected - Occurrence count
Record fault codes in aircraft maintenance log.
Refer to fault isolation manual (DMC-AMPEL360-31-00-00-730A) for corrective actions.
CAUTION: Clear fault codes only after verifying fault cause and performing corrective action.
Access fault code menu and select fault to clear.
Press CLEAR FAULT button.
Confirm clear operation when prompted.
If fault immediately recurs, fault condition still present. Do not repeatedly clear without resolving root cause.
Document fault clearing action in aircraft maintenance records.
